title: After thieves nearly emptied Tonito's Hot Wheels library, Laredo answered with hundreds of toy cars
excerpt: A free toy-car library in West Laredo honoring 10-year-old Jose Antonio Campos III was nearly emptied over the weekend. Within about an hour of the family's Facebook post, donations of toy cars started pouring in from families, businesses, collectors and car clubs.
content:
A free toy-car library in West Laredo built in memory of a 10-year-old boy was nearly emptied by a thief over the weekend — and then refilled by the community, according to Parade, reporting on KGNS News coverage.

The library, known as Tonito's Hot Wheels, sits outside the Campos family home at 4002 Eagle Pass Avenue, near the corner of Eagle Pass Avenue and Ugarte Street. It honors Jose Antonio Campos III, lovingly called Tonito, who died in December 2024 after a sudden and aggressive battle with leukemia, according to KGNS. Tonito was a fifth-grade student at Farias Elementary who loved Hot Wheels, football, mariachi, fishing and spending time outdoors.

The family said the toy car collection was full on Friday night. When they checked the library on Saturday morning, only a handful of cars remained. The family shared surveillance footage online that they said showed someone taking the cars at about 6 a.m. Saturday, Parade reported.

The loss hit the family hard, because the library was built to bring happiness to neighborhood children. But the response came fast: after the family posted about what happened on Facebook, donations started arriving within about an hour. Families, local businesses, toy collectors and car clubs stepped forward to help restock the shelves, and some parents brought their children along to donate cars of their own. For some of those families, it was their first visit to the little library.

“Because we did it to bring happiness, smiles to kids. It’s doing that. Plus, it’s teaching them a lesson in generosity, which is what Tonito, his essence was,” said Melissa Escobedo, Tonito’s aunt.

The library runs on a simple rule children can understand: leave a car, take a car. Visitors bring a die-cast toy car and exchange it for another one, so children can enjoy different cars while making sure other kids also have a chance to take one home. The family described it as Laredo’s first die-cast car library and the second of its kind in Texas.

What started as a small handmade box has grown into a bigger community project. A local car club helped build a larger display, and collectors from as far away as Live Oak have sent donations. Neighbors have also supported the library by leaving stickers, bubbles and treats for children who visit.

Even after losing so much of the collection, the family continues to welcome visitors and donations. The library remains free and open to anyone willing to trade a car and help keep the shelves stocked.

Sources: Parade reporting on KGNS News coverage (Nov. 12, 2026); KGNS News reporting on Tonito’s Hot Wheels (Nov. 9–10, 2026).
